readyBoundedGates.latestIncrement: graph.expand_neighborhood now converts failure of its direct read-only Neo4j fallback into the existing byte-capped stable response shape with empty nodes/edges/sourceRefs/graphPaths/neighbors, confidence=0, bounded error text, center, and maxHops. turbovec.rank_chunks now has capped query/sourceRefs/score-map schemas and shared byte-capped output; its deterministic score formula, result limit, and non-fusion role are unchanged. engram.chat_memory_recent now bounds userId/sourceRefs, uses the existing canonical READ ONLY transaction with 2.5-second statement_timeout, retains its row limits, and byte-caps success/error output. hypergraph.search, hypergraph.get_edge, hypergraph.expand_members, and knowledge.get_minified_map now use a 5-second upstream deadline, 256-KiB streamed JSON cap, and shared 128-KiB MCP output cap. knowledge.get_minified_map also uses the canonical READ ONLY query budget for its bounded Postgres read. clusters.get_members now trims and bounds clusterKey and limit, executes through the canonical READ ONLY transaction with a 2.5-second statement timeout, and applies the shared 128-KiB output cap. codebase.rg_search now validates bounded query/glob/context inputs, invokes rg with execFile argument arrays rather than a shell string, applies a 10-second timeout and 128-KiB maxBuffer, and clips UTF-8 output at a codepoint boundary. search.postgres_fts now bounds query/class/result count, executes through the canonical READ ONLY query-budget wrapper with a 2.5-second statement timeout, and caps success/error output at 128 KiB; search.hybrid remains model-backed and was not changed or invoked. trace.explain_retrieval now validates a 512-character query, scans at most ten pages/500 keys, selects at most twenty sorted and deduplicated keys for bounded reads, checks stored value length and fetches at most 64 KiB per value, applies a 2.5-second per-command timeout and an 8-second total deadline, and returns through the shared 128-KiB output cap. kb.search_notecards now caps query length/results and MCP output; the shared JSONL reader rejects corpora above 64 MiB/30,000 cards, rows above 256 KiB, and rank files above 4 MiB.
